title: Common uncountable nouns
subtitle: money, advice, news, furniture
summary: Learn the everyday nouns you cannot count - money, advice, news, luggage, weather - and use them correctly.

lesson.heading: Countable and uncountable

left.label: Countable
left.text: You can count them: one, two, three. They have a plural.

right.label: Uncountable
right.text: You cannot count it. There is no plural and no *a / an*.

lesson.note: We say *three suitcases*, but not ~~three luggages~~.

lesson.heading: Everyday uncountable nouns
rows: He can give some useful **information** about Bangkok.
I'll give you some **advice** about your future.

lesson.heading: Food and drink
lesson.text: A lot of uncountable nouns are kinds of food and drink. We use *some* with them, not *a* or *an*.

lesson.heading: How much do you want?
lesson.text: To say how much we want, we put a countable word in front: *two loaves of ...*, *three litres of ...*, *a kilo of ...*

lesson.heading: Grammar: a singular verb
lesson.text: An uncountable noun always takes a **singular** verb: *is*, *was*, *has*. This is true even when the word ends in *-s*, like **news**.

examples.text: The **news is** not very good today.
Their furniture **is** very old and very beautiful.
The east of the country usually **has** better weather than the west.

lesson.text: When you learn a new noun, write it down in a phrase that shows if it is countable or uncountable: *an apple* / *some advice*.

exercises.prompt: I'd like to buy a car but I haven't got enough ___.
exercises.explanation: Money is uncountable: some money, not ~~a money~~.

exercises.prompt: If you don't know what to do, ask your parents for some ___.
exercises.explanation: Advice is uncountable: some advice, not ~~an advice~~.

exercises.prompt: The ___ at the seaside is very good for you.
There is always a lot of ___ in central London.
exercises.explanation: Traffic is uncountable: a lot of traffic.

exercises.prompt: Rob left school last month and is now looking for ___.
exercises.explanation: Work is uncountable. A job is countable.

exercises.prompt: Match each adjective with the uncountable noun it goes with.
Is each noun countable or uncountable?
Accommodation in the city centre ___ expensive.
exercises.explanation: Uncountable nouns take a singular verb.

exercises.prompt: The weather in Scotland ___ best in the autumn.
exercises.explanation: Weather is uncountable, so the verb is singular: is.

exercises.statement: The news are not very good today.
exercises.explanation: The news is not very good today. News is uncountable and takes a singular verb.
Spaghetti is uncountable, so we say this spaghetti, not these spaghetti.

exercises.statement: I must find some new accommodation soon.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Accommodation is uncountable, so we say some new accommodation.

exercises.prompt: Offer to help a friend with a problem.
exercises.answer: Let me give you some advice.
